$comment: ACKNOWLEDGED findings for rendered-storage-claims.ts.
WHAT AN ENTRY IS. Not a suppression -- a dated, keyed, reasoned record that a finding is
TRUE and is not being fixed in the change that discovered it. Every acknowledged finding is
still counted in the totals the report prints; what the entry buys is a non-red gate, never
a smaller number.
KEYED BY IDENTITY, NEVER BY LINE. `key` is the finding's own stable identity (claim id, or
app + rendered PVC name). A file that grows a line cannot silently re-arm or re-suppress a
different defect.
`observed` PINS WHAT WAS ACKNOWLEDGED. It is compared byte-for-byte against the live finding.
If forgejo starts rendering 40Gi instead of 20Gi, its entry stops covering it and the gate
goes red -- because what was excused was a specific measured defect, not a name. A baseline
that keeps matching after the thing it excused has moved is the vacuity class with a filename.
`liftsWhen` IS REQUIRED. An acknowledgement with no stated exit is a permanent exemption
wearing a temporary word, and the loader refuses one without it.
STALE ENTRIES FAIL. An entry matching nothing is a claim about the tree that stopped being
true, and it is refused exactly like a catalogue row matching no claim.
WHAT IS LEFT ON `findings`. This file opened with three live-defect entries: hindsight (2) and nats
(1) were inert valuesObject paths, declarations that never reached the chart. Both manifests were
fixed on 2026-08-22, the render re-measured, and all three entries DELETED rather than left to match
nothing -- a baseline entry that outlives its defect is itself a finding, and a stale one fails this
loader in its own right. The 18 `undeclared` entries are PVCs on the non-longhorn class the ladder
does not claim to govern, listed with their sizes so the 269 GiB they represent is never invisible.
`arc-runner-set/model-cache` is the one live defect left: 100 GiB declared against a PVC nothing
renders, because the manifest declaring it is orphaned.
`unrenderable` IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE. It held FIVE entries on 2026-08-21 -- five
Applications the checker could not look at at all, which is strictly worse than any finding: a
finding is a measured disagreement, an unrenderable app is 0 bytes of evidence, and 106 GiB of
declared storage sat behind them. All five are gone, and NOT ONE was a limitation of `helm template`:
headscale       mounted its declared 3 GiB at /data, a path the chart never writes to, while the
node database and BOTH private keys sat on the container's ephemeral layer -- and
omitted the accessMode the chart hard-requires, so it templated nothing.
oz              pinned a chart version no registry has ever served, which was itself MASKING a
missing `clientApi.advertisedHost` (required by every published version) and an
`adminSecret:` block the chart has no key for.
gitlab          was missing the one `configureCertmanager` value its own sibling in the other
cluster tree already carried.
arc-runner-set  the `lookup` one, and the one that LOOKED like a limit of the tool. The chart
ships an explicit escape hatch its own error message recommends.
temporal        pointed its datastore at a CockroachDB that was already in the tree.
Every one would have failed inside ArgoCD in exactly the same place, on the same line. An empty list
here means 53 of 53 Applications were rendered and compared -- not that nothing was checked.
`observed` IS LOAD-BEARING ON **BOTH** LISTS AS OF 2026-08-22, and on `unrenderable` it was not
before. There it pins the FAILURE CLASS -- `helm-pull-failed` (the pin names nothing upstream serves)
versus `helm-template-failed` (the chart is there, our values are wrong) -- so an entry stops covering
an app whose class changes. Until then the field was required by the loader, written on every entry,
and read by NOTHING. Two agents found the same hole from opposite sides on the same day (one retiring
temporal's entry, one retiring four others) and the checks were folded into one implementation with
both sets of falsifiers kept. The stale half then earned itself immediately: merging main mid-change
re-introduced four retired acknowledgements, and it was the stale check -- not a human reading a diff
-- that refused them.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, deliberately: a `structurally-unrenderable` class. It was considered -- a chart
that calls `lookup` genuinely cannot be answered offline, and recording that as a limit of the tool
rather than as a defect would be the honest thing IF an app were in it. Measurement says none is.
Creating the class anyway, with no member, would be a category that cannot fail, which is the thing
this whole file refuses. The distinction is carried by the reason codes instead, where it is checked.

findings.reason: MEASURED DEFECT, AND THE FIRST TIME IT COULD BE MEASURED AT ALL. gha-runner-scale-set 0.12.1 renders a ServiceAccount, a Role, a RoleBinding and one AutoscalingRunnerSet -- and NO PersistentVolumeClaim. The 100 GiB `arc-model-cache` claim lives in a hand-written manifest, full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications/arc-runner-set/model-cache-pvc.yaml, that NO Application applies: the root App-of-Apps includes only '{*/Application.yaml,Application.yaml}', and arc-runner-set's own Application sources a REMOTE chart, so it cannot apply its own sibling file. The catalogue's bringUpNote has said this since it was written; what is new is that the CHECKER now says it, out of a render, instead of being unable to look -- until 2026-08-22 this app was UNRENDERABLE (its chart calls `lookup` to discover the controller ServiceAccount), so the single largest row in the ladder was reported as unchecked, and unchecked hid the fact that it is also WRONG. The consequence is not only accounting: the Application ships minRunners: 1 mounting claimName arc-model-cache, so the warm runner stays Pending on a PVC that does not exist. NOT repaired here, because the repair is a choice between two different fixes -- add a git-path Application for the PVC, or move the claim into a volumeClaimTemplate -- and neither belongs inside the change that made it visible.
findings.liftsWhen: an Application actually applies model-cache-pvc.yaml (a sibling git-path Application, or a root include that reaches it) so `arc-model-cache` appears in the render -- OR the row is retired together with the orphaned manifest, and the 100 GiB leaves the ladder honestly instead of by omission
findings.observed: declares 100Gi on "zeta-shared" x1 pods, but rendering full-ai-cluster/arc-runner-set produces NO PersistentVolumeClaim matching /^arc-model-cache$/ — the row governs a path that does not exist, and its 100 GiB are counted against nothing

findings.reason: OUT OF THE LADDER'S DECLARED SCOPE, AND THE SCOPE IS NOW MEASURABLY UNDER-STATED. storage-profiles.json says 'one row per `longhorn` PVC claim in the tree', and this claim lands on `zeta-local-path` -- the cluster default StorageClass (full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/local-storage.nix), a node-local hostPath class with reclaimPolicy: Delete. It is still real disk on the box being provisioned, so it is recorded here rather than filtered out: the rendered zeta-local-path total is 301 GiB (225 in full-ai-cluster, 76 in the infra tree). RE-DERIVED AGAIN 2026-08-22: it read 193 GiB until full-ai-cluster/gitlab became RENDERABLE. That app was missing one value (`global.ingress.configureCertmanager: false`) so it templated nothing at all, which meant its 76 GiB was counted nowhere -- not as declared, not as undeclared, not as debt. It was never absent from the disk, only from the arithmetic. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-22: it read 201 GiB (125 + 76) until hindsight's postgres moved off the default class onto longhorn, taking 8 GiB with it. single-node-budget.json's $comment_nodeDiskGib prints BOTH this figure and the readiness extractor's, and every figure in that prose is now machine-checked (findLedgerFigureDrift). UPDATED 2026-08-22: the extractor's reading is 95 GiB, not 103 -- the 8 GiB platform `Blueprint` over-count is FIXED (a Blueprint is skipped unless some Deployable names it), and it now resolves a blank storageClassName to the cluster default instead of dropping the claim, sharing one reading of that default with this module (cluster-default-storage-class.ts). What remains is STRUCTURAL and will not close: 150 GiB of this class is claimed by charts our Applications say nothing about (gitlab 76, dapr 48, loki 20, mimir-kafka 5, mimir-alertmanager 1), so there is no key in our YAML for any extractor to read. Only the render sees them, which is why both readings are kept. RE-DERIVED 2026-09-01: it read 269 GiB (193 + 76) until full-ai-cluster/minio was REMOVED. That app's upstream project is ARCHIVED, and its 20 GiB claim on this class left with it; seaweedfs -- already present, already claiming 20 GiB on this same class -- is the blob store now, so the class total moved by exactly one app's claim and the blob-store capacity on the box did not move at all. RE-DERIVED 2026-09-01: it read 249 GiB (173 + 76) until the snapshot was RE-MEASURED against the charts already on main. Two bumps had grown this class without anything noticing, because the snapshot they are audited against was never regenerated: dapr's scheduler went 1Gi x1 -> 16Gi x3 (+47) and mimir 6.2.0 bundles a Kafka StatefulSet that claims 5Gi x1 (+5). 47 + 5 = 52, and 249 + 52 = 301. Neither is new disk discovered on the box -- both were rendered by the tree the moment those bumps merged; what was stale was the measurement, which is the failure mode this whole file exists to make loud. The acknowledgement for dapr correctly STOPPED covering its claim, because `observed` pins the size and count it was written about. THIS ENTRY'S PIN MOVED 2026-09-01: it was written against 1Gi x1 and the dapr chart bump grew the claim 48-fold to 16Gi x3. The old pin is what STOPPED the acknowledgement from silently covering the larger claim -- `observed` is compared for equality against the finding, so a grown claim re-refuses instead of inheriting an acknowledgement written about a smaller one.
findings.liftsWhen: the catalogue grows a row for this PVC's non-longhorn class, at which point the claim is covered and this entry matches nothing and fails as stale. (The second exit this entry used to name -- re-deriving single-node-budget.json's zeta-local-path figure -- was NOT an exit: that was done on 2026-08-22 and the finding is still here, because what makes it a finding is that no catalogue ROW covers the PVC, not what any comment records.)
findings.observed: the chart renders a PersistentVolumeClaim of 16Gi x3 on "zeta-block-local" (no storageClassName; cluster default) that NO catalogue row covers — 48 GiB of real disk that no profile total includes

findings.reason: OpenBao runs on `zeta-local-path`, and the storage LADDER is longhorn-only -- `budgetedStorageClasses` is exactly ["longhorn"], so there is no row for a local-path volume to occupy. Same disposition as seaweedfs, forgejo, spire and opensearch, and for the same reason. WHY LOCAL-PATH RATHER THAN LONGHORN, stated because a secret store is the last place you want to be casual: OpenBao's durability here comes from RAFT REPLICATION across voters, not from the volume underneath one of them. Replicating a raft member's disk buys a second copy of a log that already has copies, and on the dev lane there is exactly one voter anyway. On metal with three voters the argument is stronger, not weaker. LIFTS WHEN: `budgetedStorageClasses` grows a second class and the local-path volumes get a ladder of their own -- at which point this entry moves together with seaweedfs's, forgejo's and opensearch's rather than one at a time. THE AUDIT VOLUME specifically: OpenBao refuses to serve if its audit device cannot write, which is deliberate -- an unauditable secret store is worse than an unavailable one -- so this 5Gi is a liveness dependency and not a nice-to-have.

WHY THE CLASS IS zeta-local-path RATHER THAN longhorn: the index is DERIVED and re-indexable from the source of truth, so it does not earn replicated storage while 1,168 GiB of longhorn PVCs in this tree have no backup target configured at all (081M1Q0WR89087G0R0036G0T0B).
